source.prompt: How do I move customer data out of spreadsheets into a CRM without losing history?
source.note: real collected answer; brand, competitors and publishers are the specs the cycle was scored with

answer.text:
Moving historical customer data out of spreadsheets and into a CRM without losing context requires a meticulous, step-by-step approach. If done wrong, you end up with broken dates, scrambled notes, and a mess of duplicate contacts.
Here is a structured playbook to get your historical data safely across the digital finish line:
Audit and Clean Your Spreadsheet Data: Audit and Clean Your Spreadsheet Data
Delete duplicates, fix glaring formatting errors (like phone numbers or state abbreviations), and ensure every row has a unique identifier (like an email address).
Standardize columns so they match your future CRM fields (e.g., separating "Full Name" into "First Name" and "Last Name").
Map Your Historical Timeline to CRM Activities: Map Your Historical Timeline to CRM Activities
Map static fields (name, email, company) easily, but handle your historical interactions (emails, calls, meeting notes) with care.
Format past communication logs into a Notes, Activities, or Engagement history import format, ensuring timestamps are preserved.
Normalize Dates and Timestamps: Normalize Dates and Timestamps
Ensure all dates use a universal format (like YYYY-MM-DD or ISO 8601) so the CRM doesn't misinterpret past dates as "today."
Run a Small Test Import: Run a Small Test Import
Export a sample of 5 to 10 rows of your cleaned spreadsheet data and import it into a sandbox or test view of your CRM.
Verify that the historical dates, past notes, and deal stages attached to those contacts look correct and haven't collapsed into the current date.
Execute the Full Migration in Batches: Execute the Full Migration in Batches
Import your data in manageable segments (e.g., 500 to 1,000 rows at a time) rather than all at once, which makes troubleshooting failed rows much easier.
Verify and Audit Post-Import: Verify and Audit Post-Import
Check random historical records against your original spreadsheet to ensure past touchpoints, owners, and creation dates transferred intact.
